A.explanation: Too small by about a factor of 4. It results from an error in resolving tension and in the total stretched length of the cord.

B.explanation: About half the correct value. It uses strain $=1.0$ by omitting the $8.0\text{ cm}$ length of cord still between the pins from the stretched total length.

C.explanation: Vertical equilibrium gives $T \approx 2.27\text{ N}$ and strain $=0.50$ from total stretched length $24.0\text{ cm}$, giving $E \approx 2.3 \times 10^6\text{ Pa}$.

D.explanation: Too large. It can result from using the full weight $mg$ as the cord tension instead of resolving the two $30^{\circ}$ inclined tensions vertically.

hints: Notice the $60^{\circ}$ angle at the load: each side of the cord makes $30^{\circ}$ with the vertical, so resolve the two cord tensions vertically to balance the $0.40\text{ kg}$ weight.
Find the cord tension from $2T\cos 30^{\circ} = mg$. The pins are smooth, so this tension $T$ is the same throughout the cord.

Compare lengths: unstretched total is $16.0\text{ cm}$, but stretched total is $8.0\text{ cm}$ between the pins plus two $8.0\text{ cm}$ sides. Use this to get extension and strain for $E = (T/A)/(x/L)$.
walkthrough: Weight of load is $W = mg = 0.40 \times 9.81 = 3.92\text{ N}$. By symmetry the tension $T$ is the same in the two sides supporting the load.
Each side makes half of $60^{\circ}$ with the vertical, i.e. $30^{\circ}$. Vertical equilibrium gives $2T\cos 30^{\circ} = W$.
Hence $T = W/(2\cos 30^{\circ}) = 3.92/(2 \times 0.866) \approx 2.27\text{ N}$. This is the tensile force in the cord.
Unstretched total length $L = 16.0\text{ cm} = 0.160\text{ m}$. In the loaded diagram the cord still spans $8.0\text{ cm}$ between the pins plus $8.0\text{ cm}$ down each side.
So stretched total length $= 8.0 + 8.0 + 8.0 = 24.0\text{ cm}$. Extension $x = 24.0 - 16.0 = 8.0\text{ cm} = 0.080\text{ m}$ and strain $= x/L = 0.080/0.160 = 0.50$.

Stress $= T/A = 2.27/(2.0 \times 10^{-6}) \approx 1.13 \times 10^6\text{ Pa}$. Then $E = \text{stress}/\text{strain} \approx 1.13 \times 10^6/0.50 \approx 2.3 \times 10^6\text{ Pa}$ with unit $\text{Pa}$. This is option C.
